<reason>CON won on feasibility plus sufficiency. Inhabited-territory distinction, Ilulissat rejection, and Russian second-strike bastion made Antarctic demilitarization/claims-freeze look unratifiable and undesirable, while Barents 2010, Polar Code, SAR/spill deals gave concrete existing governance. PRO's offshore-only adaptation and 1959 urgency blunted but never solved the ratification veto or deterrence problem.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Pressure on Russian deterrent and Ilulissat no-to-yes was decisive: A's Q1/Q2 exposed that treaty needs signatures of states that refused it and would surrender survivable deterrent, and B's A1/A2 reply about capping a race it cannot afford and deadlock forcing yes was vague versus A's concrete Barents/Polar Code/CLCS answers.</best_rebuttal>
